description:
FILED s512 (s510c resume, Opus 5.5, 2026-10-08) while chasing the s510c board "regression" on Text-Balanced t/05_extmul.t (= #2067, see there).

SILENT WRONG, pre-existing on main 3ea47a41: a write through $_[0] inside a sub with a `$` prototype does not reach the caller's variable.

    sub f ($) { $_[0] .= "x" }
    sub f2 { $_[0] .= "x" }
    sub g2 { f2($_[0]) }
    my $u = "b"; f($u); my $v = "c"; f2($v); my $w = "d"; g2($w); print "$u $v $w\n";
    perl: bx cx dx      PCL (base 3ea47a41 and s510c tree): b cx dx

The prototyped call site emits `(pl-f $u)` / `(pl-h (p-scalar (p-aref-argbox @_ 0)) "")` -- the `$` slot passes a value, not the box, so @_ is not an alias (perl: a `$` prototype imposes scalar context but $_[0] still aliases a scalar lvalue argument).  Probe: s510c worktree scratch/s510c/tb/p7.pl, p8.pl.

THIS IS THE ROOT OF #2067 / #1512 (05_extmul.t's heap exhaustion): Text::Balanced's $def_func closures are `sub { extract_variable($_[0], '') }` and extract_variable is `(;$$)`; it takes `\$_[0]` and _succeed sets pos() on that -- a COPY, so extract_multiple's FIELD loop (`while (pos($$textref) < length $$textref)`) never advances, `next FIELD` pushes '$var' forever, and the heap fills at line 117 (`extract_multiple($text)` with the default functions).  Proven with an instrumented copy of Balanced.pm (a loop guard dies after 50 iterations: pos=0, fields=$var|$var|...) on BOTH base and tree.  How many of the first 30 rows survive depends only on whether SBCL's heap exhausts during allocation (handled, stdout flushed: 16/14) or during GC (fatal, buffered stdout lost: 0/0).

Fix site: the prototype-slot argument lowering in Pl/ (the `$` slot wraps its argument in p-scalar / passes the value); a scalar LVALUE argument (a scalar variable, $_[N], an element) should pass its box under a `$` slot, as an unprototyped call does.  Bar: p8.pl == perl; a Pl/t guard row; then 05_extmul.t should run to its full 96-row plan instead of exhausting the heap.


MEASURED FURTHER (same session): under PCL_OPT=none p8.pl == perl (bx cx dx) and p7.pl reads "a bx" (perl "axy bx").  So TWO halves: (1) a prototyped sub gets NO sub_info (Parser2 ~line 2107: `if (defined(my $proto = $self->_proto_or_sig_str($sub)))` ... `next`), hence no writes_args fact, hence no arg-to-writer boxing event at its call sites, and raw-slot keeps the caller variable RAW -- the write lands on the callee-side copy; (2) a `$` slot wraps an lvalue argument in p-scalar (`(pl-h (p-scalar (p-aref-argbox @_ 0)) "")`), a copy even with every optimisation off.  Text::Balanced hits (2).


=== RULED s513 (Fable, 2026-10-08) ===
Probed vs perl 5.40.3 on main 416c710a (code 8480f3f9): ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s513/review/p2860/ (p.pl 16 rows, q.pl 6 rows; perl.txt / main.txt / main-none.txt).  perl ALIASES under every spelling -- ($), ($$), (\$), none, &-call, (;$), (;$$)-with-\$_[0], a hash element, an array element, a chain; PCL copies under every prototyped one.  The two halves CONFIRMED and separated by PCL_OPT=none: half 1 (no sub_info -> no writes_args fact -> raw-slot value) explains g / g2 / amp-g / assign and vanishes under PCL_OPT=none; half 2 (the p-scalar wrap on an element argbox at ExprToCL ~2880) explains helem / aelem / expr / chain and the Text::Balanced closure shape (q.pl closure->proto, plain->proto: the callee sees pos 2, the caller pos undef) and is independent of PCL_OPT.  The pos rows of q.pl (v1 void, v2 scalar: $_[0] =~ /x/g then pos($_[0]) undef in an UNPROTOTYPED sub) are #1567, not this task.
RULING: fixed as its OWN batch s513a (brief briefs-and-rules-for-claude-subagents/s513/s513a-prompt.md; task IDs 2900-2919; gen v2-4580), merged BEFORE s510c, so s510c then rebases across it and its board reads 0 NEW / 0 LOST with 05_extmul.t running on both base and tree -- not inside s510c (a different mechanism; s510c's corpus-diff claim "pure wrapper loss" and its bars stand only while its code is unchanged), and not accepted as a board move (16 rows lost to a GC-vs-allocation heap accident on top of a silent wrong of the prototype family).  not-supported.md line ~958 already said the element case was "extendable via the same argbox accessors if real code needs them": Text::Balanced is the real code.
